title: 报道：PlayStation 取消 Fairgames，无开发者被裁
content:
Report: Fairgames cancelled, but Haven Studios remains
Console
PC
Production
Business
News
Report: PlayStation's Fairgames cancelled, no devs to be laid off
After being announced in 2023, the online multiplayer shooter will never see the light of day, according to a new report.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 11, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
via PlayStation
Fairgames
(stylized as
FAIRGAME$
), a long in-development multiplayer shooter from internal developer Haven Studio, has been cancelled, according to
a new report from Bloomberg
. But despite the cancellation, Haven Studios will not be suffering any job cuts, according to a Sony spokesperson, as the developer will shift to a support role for other PlayStation studios.
The debut title from Haven,
Fairgames
was announced in May 2023
during a PlayStation showcase, led by creative director and Haven co-founder Mathieu Leduc. Leduc had also served as art director for Ubisoft titles
Assassin's Creed 2
,
Watch Dogs
, and
Watch Dogs 2
, worked on two unannounced and cancelled projects for Electronic Arts and Google Stadia, then founded Haven alongside veteran producer Jade Raymond in 2021.
The studio was acquired by PlayStation in 2022 with
Fairgames
as its only project, only for it to largely disappear from the public eye after its 2023 reveal. The cancellation has been the first news about the game in over three years.
Related:
PlayStation 5 crosses 100 million consoles sold
The Bloomberg story notes that
Fairgames
was part of a PlayStation initiative to produce a number of live-service games, which has resulted in a mountain of canceled projects and very few successes, with some even being pulled shortly after release like
Concord
. Multiple studios have been closed under the PlayStation umbrella in the past few years due to cancellations from this initiative, including
Bluepoint
and
London Studio
.
